A system hosts such features iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0 (cited as Rosas et al. 2020, Theorem 1), and Syn⁽ᵏ⁾ = D⁽ᵏ⁾ + G⁽ᵏ⁾ (downward causation plus causal decoupling). | [NOTE-020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-020.md) v2 | Emergence as the conversion of information | Varley and Hoel apply a PID, with the Williams–Beer I_min redundancy, to past→future mutual information and summarise it with a new layer-weighted "synergy bias" B_syn ∈ [0,1]. | [NOTE-134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-134.md) v2 | Carroll — Reality as a vector in Hilbert space | A programmatic essay, not a result paper. Carroll argues that a quantum theory is fixed, up to unitary equivalence, by the Hamiltonian's eigenvalue list {E_n} on a finite-dimensional factor (he assumes a non-degenerate spectrum), and that parts are not given. Subsystems (tensor factorisations H = H_S ⊗ H_E or ⨂_α H_α), classicality and space are to be selected afterwards as rare structure that suits the dynamics. The only uniqueness he reports is for local factorisations, and it rests on a cited theorem (Cotler et al. 2019). The system/environment criterion rests on "simple numerical examples" in a companion paper, the metric and Einstein's equation on "optimistic assumptions", and emergent fields on a hope. | Read |
| [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md) | Baedke — The Organism (Cambridge Element) | The organism is a "nexus concept" whose organizational (inward) and relational (outward) dimensions have to be integrated. Baedke argues this is best done by treating organisms as "overcomers" — agents that deliberately destabilize and reorganize their own organization — and not merely as self-maintaining "persisters". That lets organism-centred biology individuate organisms as distinct causal agents without replacing gene-centred biology. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-151.md) v2 | Register — The Depth of the Body | Register argues that body parthood "for moral purposes" is bounded below by depth. Depth is the microphysical commitment of an object's real definition, and objects that are "too deep" (a water molecule, the parcel of matter now composing the heart, a particular cloud server) are not body parts, though they are parts in the ordinary sense. His two principles ("bodily interests/rights are high-level") say that events which are high-level neutral do not bear on bodily rights or interests. So a BCI user's implemented software can be a body part owned by the user while the third-party server that runs it is not. | Read |
| [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md) v2 | SEP — Mereology | The entry argues that no mereological principle, not even the partial-order core M (Reflexivity, Transitivity, Antisymmetry), is merely a fixing of the meaning of "part". It lays out the ladder M ⊂ MM (+Supplementation) ⊂ EM (+Strong Supplementation) ⊂ GEM (+Unrestricted Sum). GEM is "virtually" a complete Boolean algebra with zero removed, and it is reached from M by exactly three adequate pairings: Supplementation + Unrestricted Sum2, Strong Supplementation + Unrestricted Sum3, and Complementation + Unrestricted Sum1. The influential Simons (1987) pairing, Supplementation + Unrestricted Sum3, which the entry's own 2003 edition also used, does not yield GEM. | Read |
